Hi, 

I have this data from a months of camera trapping. Its been manually entered into the excel arc. I was wondering if you think its possible to make kernel density estimations of the species different diel activity with this data and using your package ?

The aim is to get the effects of human activity through temporal and spatial analyses to asses wether there is more activity day/night and wether there is more activity (trapping of animals) at the stations that are further away from human activity. Perhaps by dividing the camera station into close and far from human activity (under x meters --> high human activity vice versa). messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Re: How to make kernel density estimation of species diel activity?
parts:
Hi,

the function activityOverlap() in camtrapR can help you. It uses the overlap package internally, but does a few steps for you (e.g. convert time to radial time). Run:

examples(activityOverlap)

to see a few examples. Please also see vignette 4 for details:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/camtrapr4.html#Visualising_species_activity_data

If you wish to use overlap directly, the function in overlap is called overlapPlot.

Your table seems to contain the necessary information, even though I'm slightly confused by the start and end time columns. The function will require you to use only one time columns.

Best,

Jürgen
